# Plan Creation and Organization

## Location and ownership

Save requested implementation plans under `plans/YYYYMMDD-HHmm-<topic>/` in the target project. Obtain the timestamp from the local runtime. Follow an existing project convention or reuse the supplied plan directory when revising a plan. Do not overwrite an unrelated plan with a colliding name; choose a distinct suffix.

A coordinating agent with write access persists the plan. A read-only planner returns proposed file paths and complete contents to that agent. If no writer is available, disclose the limitation rather than claiming files were saved. Respect an explicit user request for inline-only output.

## File layout

```text
plans/YYYYMMDD-HHmm-feature-name/
├── plan.md
├── phase-01-data-model.md
├── phase-02-api-and-ui.md
└── phase-03-verification.md
```

This is an example, not a mandatory phase list. Create one file for each meaningful phase of the actual task. A small plan may need one phase. Avoid empty phases or automatically adding setup, onboarding or project-management work. Create `research/`, `reports/` or `scout/` only when producing those artifacts.

## Overview: plan.md

Keep the overview concise, preferably under 80 lines. Include the goal, scope and exclusions, key decisions, dependencies, assumptions and unresolved questions. Add a table with each phase's status and a relative Markdown link to its file, for example a link labeled Data model pointing to `phase-01-data-model.md`. Keep phase details in the linked files.

## Phases: phase-NN-name.md

Include the information needed to execute that phase:

- Scope, dependencies and current status.
- Relevant context or research links.
- Files to create, modify or delete, with the reason for each change. Mark proposed paths as proposed when they do not exist yet.
- Requirements and architecture decisions where relevant.
- Ordered implementation steps and todo checkboxes.
- Acceptance criteria and concrete verification commands or observable checks.
- Material risks, security considerations and rollback steps where relevant.

Follow project instructions and applicable development rules. Do not pad small phases with empty headings. Phase links are relative to the phase file, not to the project root.

## Verification and handoff

Read back the saved overview and phases. Check that every phase link resolves and dependencies agree with execution order. Return the real overview path and summarize the phases. Leave pending work pending; update status only when its acceptance criteria have been verified.
